choices: C1 offset sign: h = host clock - server clock (the lab's offset_ns, scenario.rs:930, :1131); error = estimate - h, reported as abs.

C2 integer ns throughout, as the code: L1's uniform integer delay in [one_way - a, one_way + a] inclusive (l1/src/lib.rs:846), the client's floor step grid (client/src/lib.rs:485-488), the server's floor tick grid floor(k*1e9/30) (schedule.rs:125-134); one division at the end.

C3 per-sample own-ping estimate: NTP/Cristian midpoint est = (c_s + c_r)/2 - s_hat, so est - h = (d_down - d_up)/2 + (s_r - s_hat) [+ b/2 bitten]; RTT = c_r - c_s, hold 0 (pump.rs:460, the runner wakes at the arrival).
C4 half-tick bias: every tick-stamp estimator (mean, lowest-RTT, newest) uses the centred stamp (T_{k-1} + T_k)/2; the uncentred T_k is a printed sensitivity only (about -16.6 ms median, fails).

C5 a Ping arriving exactly at a tick instant is stamped that tick (RQ8: the I/O step before the tick at one instant, scenario.rs:6-11, :476); stamp = smallest k with T_k >= s_r. 0 of 60,000 samples hit it under (ii).
C6 exact sub-tick stamp (U4F-Q6 (b), addition): the server arrival floored to the us since the previous tick's due instant.

C7 phases: per connect phi uniform in [0, 33,333,333] ns, first ping at T_300 + phi, ping m at step 3m = exactly m*1e8 ns later, so under (ii) every ping meets the tick grid at exactly phi (no ns drift on the floor grid); (i) shifts the quantising grid per sample by a uniform u_m, everything else unchanged.

C8 room-ping schedule: one seeded start R0 uniform in [0, 250 ms) per connect, 8 pings exactly 250 ms apart (pump slip left out), the same under (i) and (ii); since 250 ms = 7.5 ticks their phase against the client grid alternates by half a tick. (e)'s rows are therefore identical under (i) and (ii).

C9 (e) combination left open by the brief, both reported as main rows: e/mean-of-8 (mean of the 8 per-ping estimates) and e/lowest-of-8 (the ping with the smallest arrival - sent_ns); one-way delay = half the lowest observed own-ping RTT (bitten under arrivals (2)).

C10 the bite: every arrival stamp (own Pongs and room pings) moved to the first client step at or after it (an arrival at a step instant is read by that step: poll_recv(now) includes now); bitten RTTs become exactly 3 ticks = 100,000,000 ns (3,000 of 3,000 connects); lowest-RTT ties broken by first minimum in send order (strict <).

C11 loss: P2's 2 % each way not in the main rows (D4 fixes 20 samples and 8 room pings); run as an addition (own sample kept at 0.98^2, room ping at 0.98). Not modelled: L1's 1 % reorder step (it only delays, never lowers a lowest-RTT pick), the ADR's drift/reset filter rules, the read-instant cut (all samples arrive before it), and any constant between room tick numbers and server ns (the model gives the client the exact tick-to-ns map).
C12 draws: one random.Random(seed) per seed 1, 2, 3; a fixed number of draws per connect in a fixed order, so every variant is paired on the same draws; h uniform in [0, 1,000 s) as the lab.
C13 the bite shows when clean p99 <= 5 ms and bitten p99 > 5 ms, judged pooled (3,000) and per seed (all three agree); p99 nearest-rank ceil(0.99 n) as the judge (judge/src/eval.rs:264-289).

C14 additions marked addition=true: mean and lowest-RTT with the exact stamp; the newest sample (own ping 19, always the last to arrive) with the tick stamp and with the exact stamp; 2 % loss rows (the exact-stamp ones in this schema; all loss rows are in the notes).

summary:
I built the independent model B of brief row D4 and ran it once (/home/user/Shamble-Frontlines/.checkpoints/netcode-proof-test/u4f-r3/d4b/d4_model_b.py; the full output and choices C1 to C14 are in d4b-notes.md beside it). I did not read the main session's d4/ folder. It uses D4's fixed parameters at P2 (each direction 50 ms + U[-10, 10] ms, in integer ns), 1,000 connects x seeds 1, 2, 3, 20 own pings and 8 room pings. p99 is nearest-rank, as the judge computes it.

(1) As built (U4F-Q6 (a)), no estimator passes -47's 5 ms under either phase model. With the stamp centred on the tick (C4), the mean of samples gives 6.134 ms (i) and 8.831 ms (ii); the lowest-RTT sample gives 18.391 ms and 18.281 ms. NA-4 holds: phase-locking raises the mean's p99 from 6.1 to 8.8 ms (max 11.3 ms). Even uniform phases miss the bar, because 20 samples of a 33.3 ms quantisation leave about 2.3 ms of spread. If the stamp is not centred, every estimator also carries about a -16.6 ms bias.

(2) Option (e) as worded fails. The mean of the 8 room pings gives 12.712 ms with a +7.29 ms median bias, because half the lowest of 20 RTTs (about 42.7 ms) sits below the 50 ms mean one-way delay. The lowest of the 8 gives 6.424 ms. Both are the same under (i) and (ii), by construction.

(3) An exact sub-tick server stamp (U4F-Q6 (b), an addition) passes under both phase models. The mean gives 2.312 ms. The lowest-RTT sample gives 4.567 ms, a thin margin: seeds 4.740, 4.478 and 4.553 ms, and 4.871 ms on seed 3 with 2 % loss.

(4) The tick-quantised bite shows only under the exact stamp: bitten, the mean reads 12.194 ms and the lowest-RTT sample 9.922 ms, pooled and on every seed. Under the as-built tick stamp, and for (e), it is hidden because the clean runs already fail. The newest-sample bite (8.904 ms with the exact stamp) shows against both exact-stamp estimators and is hidden against every tick-stamp one.

(5) On TE-6's worry: the lowest-RTT bite still shows under the exact stamp, but only because every bitten RTT is exactly 3 ticks (3,000 of 3,000 connects) and ties go to the oldest sample. I did not model a filter that averages all the tied lowest samples; my estimate puts its bitten bias near +3.3 ms, so 5.3's short run is still needed.

(6) 2 % loss changes no pass or fail result. Not modelled: L1's reorder step, the ADR's filter thresholds, and any constant between room tick numbers and server ns.

For U4F-Q6 this is data, not a ruling: of (a), (b) and (e), only (b) lets -47 pass at P2 with both bites showing, and among (b)'s estimators the mean has the margin.
